title: Adaptive admission shaping and soft per-customer throttles for rerank endpoint
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Design and implement a SLO-driven admission control layer for the /rerank endpoint that performs per-customer soft-throttles, cost-aware admission shaping, and region-aware fallback routing. The goal is to maintain 99th-percentile latency SLOs under bursty load while preserving result quality for high-priority customers.
background: Recent incidents (see incident runbook links) showed cascading latency spikes when embedding+r eranking workloads surge from a handful of customers. Existing circuit breakers are too coarse-grained: they either cut off traffic or allow retries that overload downstream rerank replicas. We need finer-grained, admission-level controls that consider request token cost, customer tier, KV cache hit rate, and regional capacity.
proposed_solution: 1) Admission controller that computes an admission score per request using: customer_priority, estimated_token_cost (embedding + rerank), current_inflight_by_shard, and recent KV cache hit ratio. 2) Soft-throttle mechanism that returns 202 (accepted-with-delay) for low-priority requests with a hinted retry-after, and allows higher-priority requests to preempt admission slots. 3) Region-aware routing policy: if local region capacity below threshold, transparently route to secondary region with best latency estimate; fall back to cached precomputed reranks if cross-region latency would exceed SLO. 4) Simple per-customer credit bucket to rate-limit sustained heavy users and prevent noisy-neighbor effects. 5) Metric-driven configuration with defaults in runtime-1.23 and a per-customer override in Dedicated/Private.
acceptance_criteria:
- 99p tail latency for /rerank under 95th percentile request size workloads does not exceed current SLO in staged canary.
- Soft-throttle responses are emitted for at least 90% of shaped low-priority traffic instead of hard failures.
- Regional failover occurs automatically when regional capacity < 20% and results in median extra latency < 40ms for affected requests.
- No customer loses >5% of successful rerank responses during a simulated global surge test.
- Dashboard panels for admission_score, shaped_count, routed_to_secondary_region, per_customer_credit_usage are added to console-2025.02 release.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): implement admission controller runtime flags and enable for 5% of traffic in us-east-1 with a monitoring dashboard and synthetic load. Phase 2 (expanded canary): increase to 25% across US regions, enable per-customer credits for 10 paying customers to validate fairness. Phase 3 (gradual): flip default to enabled for all hosted traffic; expose per-customer soft-limit overrides in Dedicated UI and private config. Phase 4: Backfill CDN-level hints/edge cache for precomputed reranks.
monitoring_and_alerting: Add Prometheus metrics: rerank_admission_score_bucket, rerank_shaped_count_total, rerank_soft_throttle_rate, rerank_region_routed_total, rerank_credit_depleted_total. Create alert: rerank_shaped_rate > 40% for >5m AND 99p_latency > SLO -> P0 incident. Post-deploy SLO burn dashboard and daily regression alerts tied to quality evals.
open_risks:
- Mis-estimation of token_cost can starve high-value short requests.
- Per-customer credits add state that must be consistent across leader failovers.
- Cross-region routing may increase egress cost and expose PII policy constraints for Private customers.
- Soft-throttle UX may cause client confusion if SDKs don't handle 202-with-retry semantics.
Mitigations: conservative defaults, strong backward-compatibility, and integration tests for credit persistence.

decisions: Use soft-throttle (202) vs HTTP 429 to allow client SDKs to implement backoff-friendly flows
Credit store implemented in Redis with a lightweight leader-lock; move to Raft-backed store if scale requires
Default region routing to prefer local region unless estimated added latency < 30ms
